answer: Each identity claims one ferrous rivet at a wharf yard, locks a 75-credit bond keyed to that rivet, and files a quill-signed shear log with diameter and batch. The first shear test costs 30 credits; the k-th costs 30+6(k-1), so the 1,000th costs 6,024 and 1,000 fakes pay 3,027,000 in fees plus 75,000 locked. An auditor recomputes shear load from the rivet table and burns the bond on a mismatch, missing batch, or reused serial. A rented-rivet ring fails: one serial cannot pass two keys, so the second filing burns both. An honest agent pays 30 once and reclaims the bond after a clean audit.
